newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU stays silent on Boutros-Ghali veto.
newsitem.headline: OAU stays silent on Boutros-Ghali veto.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) remained tight-lipped on Thursday about the U.S. veto against Africa's candidate for the U.N.'s top job.
The pan-African body has kept a surprising silence since Tuesday's veto of U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, who is seeking a second five-year term.
Boutros-Ghali, an Egyptian, was officially endorsed as Africa's candidate at an OAU summit last July and the position has been repeated many times.

Diplomats have linked the OAU's silence with the general belief that the organisation's own secretary-general, Salim Ahmed Salim, will be a candidate for the U.N. job if Boutros-Ghali is eventually eliminated from the race.
Salim, who has previously denied that he was a candidate, returned on Thursday to OAU headquarters in the Ethiopian capital from a mission to West Africa and was not available for comment.
OAU spokesman Ibrahim Dagash and his two assistants were both away on mission or on vacation.
Salim is one of several Africans tipped as potential candidates.

A front-runner is Ghanaian Kofi Annan, a U.N. under secretary-general who heads U.N. peacekeeping operations. Ghana's Foreign Minister Obed Asamoah told Reuters on Wednesday that his country was ready to propose Annan.
The U.N. Security Council has agreed to give priority to candidates from Africa on the grounds that if Boutros is denied a second term, he should at least be followed by another African.
